text:
Ivan Barbashev spent October looking for a goal, and on Wednesday he found two of them in one night against Utah: a backdoor tap-in after Victor Olofsson fanned on a shot, and a solo dance through the Mammoth that Jesse Granger of The Athletic called an "insane individual effort." That was enough for the team's video crew to ask whether it was the goal of the year.

The slump was never about how he played. Vegas takes 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, more than nine points better than without him, and his four goals sit a touch under the 5.2 his chances deserved. He's the engine of a third line with Tomas Hertl that has been the Golden Knights' best at even strength.

Evolving-Hockey had him worth 2.2 wins last season, 42nd among forwards, though it also noted he plays with strong teammates. He draws more penalties than he takes and gets his share of the passes across the slot that turn into goals, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Twelve assists in 21 games says the rest of his game never left.
